title: Related Questions
question: Related Questions Q. Assalamu alikum Iam 76 year old muslim.I have 8 childrens totally. 4 men and 4 women. As per islamic law and indian custom i have completed my 4 daughters marriage in a grand manner(with 500 gms gold). My three son have been married and my younger son is a bachelor(till now).Me and my wife live with my sons.We all live togather in my own earned house.My sons cleared my debts when i lost my business.I gifted my house only to my 4 sons because this is the only place where my sons and my daughter-in-laws(with their childrens) live and they take care of me and my wife.Is this correct according to Islamic law. please clear my doubt. Jazakallah 1830 views Q. Share of daughter in father's property 2914 views Q. 11th October 2010 / 2nd Zul Qadah 1431 Assalamou alaikum Respected Mufti sahib, I live in England, United Kingdom. I am a widow, my husband passed away nearly 3 months ago. I have 9 sons and 2 daughters. My husband?s mother is also alive. My late husband was the owner of two houses. Some months prior to his death, my husband made me a joint owner in one of these properties. Upon the instructions of my late husband, a solicitor completed the legal paperwork and we both signed various documents in the presence of witnesses. After the death of my husband, my children requested a scholar to explain the rules of Islamic inheritance so we could distribute my husband?s wealth according to the Shariah. When the discussion arose about the joint ownership of one of the houses, the scholar was of the opinion that this transfer of joint ownership was not valid because it seemed to him that this was only done symbolically and not as a genuine gift. However, beside the legal paperwork there is no other document available to support or negate the intention of the deceased. The scholar also said that even if the above gift was genuine, this kind of gift is faasid because of the following rule of Hiba: ومن وهب شقصاً مشاعاً فالهبة فاسدةٌ، فإن قسمه وسلمه جاز ) الهداية شرح بداية المبتدي,ص225,ج3, الناشر المكتبة الإسلامية) Which in essence says, if the item is such that if it is divided it can still be of use, then it is not permissible to give it without dividing it. Such items are ?a plot of land, a big house...?. See Bahishti Zewar (link below) page 66 point 5 http://www.islamicbulletin.org/free_downloads/women/bahishti_4_5_6_7.pdf I would be grateful if you would clarify (a) whether a house in the UK falls within the category of divisible property; (b) whether according to the Shariah I am the rightful owner of 50% of the house which was in joint ownership between myself and my husband. Jazakallah 2088 views Q. With all respect I have a question in regards to a fathers wealth distribution. We could not find a ulooma whose capable of giving answers to our questions here in Fiji. I believe your instituion compromises of uloomas of high calibre. Question one: What is the true concept or shariah rulling on how a fathers wealth should be distributed among his children? Question two: Does Shariah allow a father to decide what he will give to which child? Question three: Can a father decide not to give anything to one child? Question four: What happens if the father makes a will for properties to be distributed after his death, who gets what? Question five: What percentage is to be left to the wife? Question six: Suppose if one of the son passes away does is his share from the fathers wealth suppose to be directed to his wife and kids or does his share no longer exist? Question seven: Do the girls receive equal shares as the boys? The other issue I have is can a muslim eat or drink at another muslims house who meaningly promotes and consumes haraam meat at their home, such as meat which is slaughtered against shariah practices or in other words I should say those animals who are stunned prior to slaughter or being mechanically slaughtered. Also I would like to know if a Muslim has got a practice or promotes munafiqat, and there are solid evidences of him promoting munafiqat such as hiding the truth and speaking untruthfully, can we call them a munafiq? and what are the signs of a munafiq as per Al-quran. Some of my questions may be offending but it is extremely difficult to live amongst the muslim community in Fiji and New Zealand. Your answers will make my life much easier insha-Allah. 4961 views Q. We are 3 brothers and 1 sister my father is alive alhamdullilah with grace of allah My mother has expired in 1999. My question actually is my father is having a property in hyderabad and we want to sell the property and my father is having debts upto 85 lakhs no we have fixed the value of property at 1.4 cr. kindly suggest us how to divide the sale proceeds among 3 brothers and 1 sister . My father is still alive and as per shariah what will be the percentage given to sons and daughters . one more question is as my sister is married does my brother in law have any right to ask about the share or can he demand the share . does he have any right to talk about the share at all . one more thing i would like to add is that in the debt mentioned above 18 lakhs is due to our brother in law . kindly guide us on this issue. 1940 views Q. Assalamualaikum Brother A friends mom want to write a will and give away all her wealth to a cancer charity in canada.The whole family is muslim. She has three daughters aged 22, 20 and 7. My question is that can the mother give away all her wealth in charity after she dies or even while she is alive? If the mother has permission of her two adult daughters, can she give it away then, minus the share of the little sister? Would it be okay for a muslim lady to give everything to a charity in canada instead of helping people here in pakistan where she normally resides? Is it okay for Muslims to give charity to christian or any other organisations besides muslims'? If the mother does write this will and give away everything to this cancer charity in canada without consulting with her daughters, would she be held accountable on the day of judgement, i mean is that a sin? Also please keep in mind that her husband is well off too and the mom generally has a tendency to help the needy, so please let me know whats the best possible option for her knowing that she has always wanted to help the poor and the needy. answer: Transactions & Dealings >> Inheritance & Will Question ID: 14385 Country: India Title: June 19, 2009 Assalamualaikum Wo Rahmathullahi Barkathahu, My name is Mohammed Safiulla from Bangalore, India. Kindly let me know the Fatwa in light of Quran and Sunnah. My Father in law passed away last year. May Allah reward him with a place in Jannathul firdose. Amin. Summ Amin. My deceased Father in law has two sons-one married and the other a bachelor and one daughter who is also married. I would like to know how the property that used to be owned by my deceased father in law need to be distributed. My mother in law is alive and she is taking the family pension. Also let me know whether the children have any rights in the deceased?s pension also. Also my deceased father in law has got some ancestral property from his father. Kindly let me know whether the grand children (two grand sons and a grand daughter) have got any right in this property. Please note that there is no WILL on any of the properties by my deceased Father in law. Your earliest reply would be highly appreciated. Question: June 19, 2009 Assalamualaikum Wo Rahmathullahi Barkathahu, My name is Mohammed Safiulla from Bangalore, India. Kindly let me know the Fatwa in light of Quran and Sunnah. My Father in law passed away last year. May Allah reward him with a place in Jannathul firdose. Amin. Summ Amin. My deceased Father in law has two sons-one married and the other a bachelor and one daughter who is also married. I would like to know how the property that used to be owned by my deceased father in law need to be distributed. My mother in law is alive and she is taking the family pension. Also let me know whether the children have any rights in the deceased?s pension also. Also my deceased father in law has got some ancestral property from his father. Kindly let me know whether the grand children (two grand sons and a grand daughter) have got any right in this property. Please note that there is no WILL on any of the properties by my deceased Father in law. Your earliest reply would be highly appreciated. Answer ID: 14385 Posted on: Sep 1, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 1263/1201=B/1430) The property and wealth left by your father in law will be distributed in 40 shares. Out of the 40 shares, wife will get 5 shares, each son will get 14 shares and the daughter will get 7 shares. The ancestral property owned by him will be divided in the same way. The grandchildren will have no share. Note : The family pension given by the government to the widow monthly is solely for her and no one has a right over it. Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
